description: A made-up sample lesson that uses every step type and every lab once, so the lesson player and the content checks can be tested end to end.
title: Every step, once

steps.body:
Ada sells paper lanterns, and her shop needs a small website. This sample lesson follows her site from a tap on a phone to a finished page.

It is made up, and it exists to test the lesson player: every kind of step appears once, and every lab is drawn once.
Tap through the trip and watch what moves between the phone and the server.

states.title: You type an address
states.html: You type the shop's address and tap Go.

states.title: Find the server
states.html: The browser looks up where the shop's server is.

states.title: Send a request
states.html: The browser asks the server for the page. That message is a request.

states.title: The server responds
states.html: The server sends back a response, starting with the page's HTML.

states.title: Fetch the extras
states.html: The HTML links to more files: CSS, images and JavaScript. The browser asks for each one.

states.title: Draw the page
states.html: With the files in hand, the browser draws the lantern shop on the screen.

steps.body: Ada's shop sign uses this CSS. What will the word look like when the page runs?

options.feedback: Right. A weight of 700 is bold.
Italic comes from font-style, not font-weight.
Nothing here changes the size.

hints: Look at the property name: what does weight describe in a font?
font-weight sets how thick the letters are. 400 is normal.
Example: a heading with font-weight: 800 looks extra thick.

steps.body: Try each value in the preview. Which one puts the word in the middle of the line?

options.feedback: That keeps it at the start of the line.
Yes. center puts the text in the middle.
That moves it to the end of the line.

hints: Watch where the word moves as you try each one.
text-align lines text up inside its box.
Example: a centred title sits in the middle of the page width.

steps.body: Change the gap between Ada's three lanterns.
steps.ask: Which value leaves the most space between the lanterns?

options.feedback: 0 puts them right next to each other.
Some space, but not the most.
Right. The bigger the gap, the more space.

hints: Try each value and compare the spaces.
gap sets the space between flex items.
Example: gap: 8px leaves 8 pixels between each pair of items.

steps.body: Step through the two axes of Ada's menu bar.

states.title: The main axis
states.html: In a flex row, the main axis runs left to right.

states.title: The cross axis
states.html: The cross axis runs top to bottom.

states.title: Centre on the cross axis
states.html: align-items: center lines the items up along the middle of the cross axis.

states.title: Turn it into a column
states.html: In a column the main axis runs top to bottom instead.

states.title: Centre a column
states.html: Now align-items: center works left to right.

steps.body: Load the page on a fast connection, then on a slow one, and watch the files arrive.
steps.ask: On a slow connection, which file arrives last?

options.feedback: The HTML is always the first file.
Yes. The photo is by far the biggest file.
The styling arrives early so the page can be drawn.

hints: Watch the list of files as the page loads.
Bigger files take longer on a slow connection.
Example: a news site often shows its headline before its photos.

steps.body: Step through the parts of an address for Ada's shop.

states.title: The scheme
states.html: https says how the browser and the server will talk.

states.title: The path
states.html: The path names the page on that server.

states.title: The query
states.html: The query adds details, such as a search for gold lanterns.

steps.body: Send each request to Ada's server and read the status code that comes back.

options.feedback: The home page exists, so the server answers 200 OK.
Right. 404 means the server has no page at that address.
A sent form usually gets a success code or a redirect.

hints: Try each request and read the number in the response.
Codes starting with 4 mean the request asked for something the server can't give.
Example: a link with a typo in it often leads to a 404 page.

steps.body: Ada's friend opens the shop on a weak network. The text has loaded, but the photo hasn't. What will the page show in the meantime?

options.feedback: The browser doesn't wait for every file before drawing.

options.html: The text, with a space where the photo will go
options.feedback: Right. The browser leaves space for the photo and fills it in when it arrives.
Nothing has failed. One file just hasn't arrived yet.

hints: Think about the order the files arrive in.
The browser draws with the files it already has.
Example: video sites show the page before the video starts.

steps.body: Put the trip to Ada's shop in order.
steps.wrong: Not quite. The browser has to find the server before it can ask it for anything.
hints: Start with what you do.
The browser can't ask a server it hasn't found yet.
Example: you look up a number before you call it.

steps.body: Ada wants her lantern photos to load faster on slow phones. What helps most?

options.feedback: Yes. Smaller files arrive sooner.

options.html: Add more text to the page
options.feedback: More text doesn't speed up photos.
A brighter colour doesn't change how fast files arrive.

hints: Which file was slowest in the lab?
Download time grows with file size.
Example: a 500 KB photo can often be saved at 80 KB and look the same on a phone.
Find the color property in styles.css.
Replace its value with the hex code.
Example: .title { color: #1E66F5; } makes a title blue.

steps.body: Add three lanterns to the list: red, gold and blue, one li each.

tests.name: The list has three lanterns
tests.code: assert($$('.shop li').length === 3, 'Add three li items inside the list.')

hints: Items go between the opening and closing ul tags.
Each item is its own li element.
Example: a list of two drinks has two li elements, each with a drink inside.

points: A page arrives as a request and a response, then more files.
CSS changes how the page looks, and you can try values live.
You can change starter code until every test passes.

cards.front: What does the browser send to a server?
